findings.title: HTTPS menu sends prepared and legacy configurations into address-migration-only path
findings.scenario: An initial HTTPS setup fails after retaining phase=prepared metadata, or an existing instance retains legacy Authelia HTTPS metadata. The operator retries setup from the one-stop HTTPS menu with the same address.
findings.actual: Any nonempty https-read result causes Console.https to select https-migrate. setup_https rejects prepared/legacy metadata with identity_conflict: Address migration requires an active built-in HTTPS configuration. The operator cannot recover through this menu even after the original certificate/network issue is resolved.
findings.expected: Use the ordinary HTTPS resume/legacy migration path for prepared/legacy metadata; use address migration only for eligible active builtin metadata. Preserve omitted publicOrigin when resuming a retained address: the menu currently always adds it and the ordinary resume guard compares omission explicitly.
findings.reproductionMethod: Real Console menu and parser plus real setup_https early validation; only persisted-metadata read and host/precondition boundaries stubbed. Both prepared builtin and legacy fixtures return the stated error. No network or service actions.
findings.testsGap: Existing menu test bodies were reviewed; coverage does not require successful resume of prepared/legacy HTTPS metadata through the menu.

findings.title: Provider layer requirement checks only registry default and allows advanced secondary providers in legacy mode
findings.scenario: A provider registry keeps ChatGPT as its default and contains an enabled nondefault Bedrock provider; the operator rolls back the configuration layer or resumes an old legacy-mode candidate.
findings.actual: require_provider_layer reads top-level kind, which combine projects from the default connection, and accepts layered=False. Actual ProviderStore.prepare(layered=False) writes a generation containing amazon-bedrock-runtime without requirements.toml; require_candidate_layer(targetMode=legacy) accepts that exact generation. This defeats the documented managed-layer requirement for advanced provider definitions and permits removing enforced provider requirements while they remain enabled.
findings.expected: Validate relevant registry connection kinds at every preparation, rollback, and candidate recovery guard so an enabled provider requiring system-v1 prevents legacy publication.
findings.reproductionMethod: Real provider_registry.change, ProviderStore.prepare(layered=False), and config_layer.require_candidate_layer. Files written only below .work using a synthetic API key; ownership-only directory wrappers substituted for Windows. No service or network activity.
findings.testsGap: Existing advanced-provider layer gates are single-provider checks; focused registry tests cover registry generation on legacy mode with Responses but do not reject enabled advanced secondary providers.
